_metadata.description: Consolidated literature benchmarks for DecarbIQ model validation
_metadata.usage: Pipeline reads this file in validation step. If a benchmark is missing, fall back to web search.

gas_price_forecasts.description: Independent HH natural gas price forecasts for comparison

eia_aeo_2025_reference.source: EIA Annual Energy Outlook 2025, Reference Case
eia_aeo_2025_reference.notes: Reference case assumes current laws and regulations. Range across side cases is roughly +/- $1.00.

nymex_futures_strip.source: CME/NYMEX Henry Hub Natural Gas Futures
nymex_futures_strip.notes: Futures strip is risk-neutral pricing; typically slightly below fundamental forecasts due to convenience yield.

consensus_range.description: Approximate consensus across EIA, NYMEX, IHS Markit, Wood Mackenzie

garch_parameters.description: Published GARCH(1,1) estimates for natural gas log-returns

pindyck_2004.citation: Pindyck RS (2004). Volatility and commodity price dynamics. J Futures Markets 24(11):1029-1047

sadorsky_2006.citation: Sadorsky P (2006). Modeling and forecasting petroleum futures volatility. Energy Economics 28(4):467-488

kang_2009.citation: Kang SH et al (2009). Forecasting volatility of crude oil markets. Energy Economics 31(1):119-125

efimova_2014.citation: Efimova O, Serletis A (2014). Energy markets volatility modelling using GARCH. Energy Economics 43:264-273

nick_2014.citation: Nick S, Thoenes S (2014). What drives natural gas prices? Energy Economics 44:422-431

mohammadi_2015.citation: Mohammadi H (2015). A note on GARCH effects on natural gas. Applied Economics Letters 22(13):1083-1087

literature_consensus.notes: Post-2012 (shale era) estimates tend toward lower alpha, higher beta. Full-sample including 1997-2012 yields higher alpha due to pre-shale volatility.

era_expectations.description: Expected GARCH parameter ranges by market era

pre_shale.notes: Tight supply, hurricane sensitivity, weather-driven spikes. Higher alpha (faster shock response).

post_shale.notes: Abundant shale gas supply, stable low prices. Lower alpha, higher beta (slow mean reversion of vol).

post_covid.notes: LNG exports, Russia-Ukraine war, energy transition. Intermediate vol between pre-shale and post-shale.

gas_passthrough.description: Heat-rate based gas-to-electricity price passthrough coefficients

theoretical_range.source: Standard heat rate 7-9 MMBtu/MWh for CCGT fleet

borenstein_bushnell_2015.citation: Borenstein S, Bushnell J (2015). The US Electricity Industry after 20 Years of Restructuring. Annual Review of Economics 7:437-463
borenstein_bushnell_2015.notes: Varies by market structure and renewable penetration

linn_mccormack_2019.citation: Linn J, McCormack K (2019). The roles of energy markets and environmental regulation in reducing coal-fired plant profits and electricity sector emissions. RAND J Economics 50(4):733-767

gas_passthrough.notes: Markets with high renewable penetration (CAISO, ERCOT increasingly) show lower passthrough as renewables set marginal price more often.

hurricane_frequency.description: Tropical cyclone frequency trends from major climate assessments

ipcc_ar6_2021.citation: IPCC AR6 WG1 (2021), Chapter 11: Weather and Climate Extreme Events
ipcc_ar6_2021.notes: No detectable trend in Atlantic basin frequency. Intensity increase likely but frequency flat.

knutson_2020.citation: Knutson T et al (2020). Tropical cyclones and climate change assessment. Bull AMS 101(3):E303-E322
knutson_2020.notes: Global TC frequency may decrease 0-15% by 2100. Cat4-5 proportion increases.

vecchi_2021.citation: Vecchi GA et al (2021). Changes in Atlantic major hurricane frequency since the late-19th century. Nature Communications 12:4054
vecchi_2021.frequency_trend: no significant trend after accounting for observing capabilities
vecchi_2021.notes: Apparent increase in Atlantic is primarily detection artifact.

noaa_gfdl.citation: NOAA GFDL Hurricane Research Division, Knutson 2021 summary
noaa_gfdl.key_finding: 25-30% increase in Category 4-5 intensity; 0-15% decrease in total frequency globally

emanuel_2021.citation: Emanuel K (2021). Atlantic tropical cyclones downscaled from climate reanalyses. PNAS 118(41):e2109806118
emanuel_2021.frequency_trend: no robust increase in basin-wide count

event_probabilities.description: Empirical gas-impact event rates from 29-year named event catalog (1997-2025)

geopolitical.qualifying_event: Russia-Ukraine War 2022 (+$5.00/MMBtu to HH via LNG arbitrage)
geopolitical.notes: Most geopolitical events affect European/Asian prices but not US HH directly. US is a net exporter since 2016.

demand_shock.notes: Polar vortex events have highest direct US price impact coefficient.

policy_shock.qualifying_event: Freeport LNG Fire 2022 (policy/regulatory forced shutdown, -$0.50 to HH)
policy_shock.notes: Policy events tend to have gradual rather than shock-like price impacts.

electricity_price_benchmarks.description: Historical and forecast wholesale electricity price references

historical_avg_2019_2024.notes: 2021 includes Uri. 2022 inflated by gas prices. 2023-2024 normalized. Mean excl 2021-2022: ~$27.

ercot.notes: ERCOT is energy-only market with scarcity pricing. Long-run average ~$30-40/MWh in normal gas price environments.

historical_avg_2019_2024.notes: 2022 inflated by gas price spike. CAISO includes carbon cost (CA cap-and-trade ~$30-35/ton). Mean excl 2022: ~$41.

caiso.notes: CA carbon allowance adds ~$8-12/MWh. Battery storage growth (0→15 GW 2018-2025) is deflationary for peak prices.

mean_reversion_parameters.description: Literature estimates for commodity price mean-reversion speed

schwartz_1997.citation: Schwartz ES (1997). The stochastic behavior of commodity prices: Implications for valuation and hedging. J Finance 52(3):923-973
schwartz_1997.notes: Natural gas at the faster end due to storage/production flexibility

pilipovic_2007.citation: Pilipovic D (2007). Energy Risk: Valuing and Managing Energy Derivatives. 2nd ed. McGraw-Hill
pilipovic_2007.notes: Natural gas mean-reverts faster than oil due to storage costs and seasonal demand

consensus_natural_gas.notes: Current model uses kappa=0.15/month (half-life ~4.6 months) — within range

production_economics_floor.description: Minimum gas prices implied by production economics
production_economics_floor.notes: Below ~$1.50/MMBtu, producers shut in wells. The MC model should enforce a floor near this level to prevent unrealistic P5/P10 values.
production_economics_floor.source: EIA Drilling Productivity Report, various operator 10-K filings

price_impact.notes: Each 1 bcfd of LNG exports adds ~$0.12/MMBtu to HH. Total impact from 14→25 bcfd = ~$1.30/MMBtu

battery_storage_capacity.description: US utility-scale battery storage deployment trajectory
battery_storage_capacity.source: EIA Annual Energy Outlook 2025, BNEF New Energy Outlook 2024
battery_storage_capacity.texas_reference_note: EIA AEO + BNEF consensus. Modo Energy reports 13.9 GW operational Jan 2026, 40-55 GW by 2029 — higher than EIA/BNEF baseline. Model projects independently from data; literature serves as validation check.

price_impact.mechanism: Reduces gas peaker dispatch, compresses peak-to-off-peak spread
price_impact.notes: Each GW of 4-hour storage displaces ~1 GW of gas peaker capacity. Deflationary for peak electricity prices.

carbon_emission_factors.description: EPA eGRID emission factors by fuel type for carbon intensity computation
carbon_emission_factors.notes: Coal includes sub-bituminous and bituminous. Gas CCGT is marginal fleet average. Other includes biomass, geothermal.

generation_mix_benchmarks.description: EIA AEO 2025 reference case generation shares for cross-check
generation_mix_benchmarks.notes: Ranges reflect reference case +/- side cases. ERCOT coal retirement trend suggests 0% by mid-2030s.

grid_reliability_benchmarks.description: NERC/ERCOT reliability planning standards and recent metrics
grid_reliability_benchmarks.source: NERC Long-Term Reliability Assessment 2024, ERCOT CDR
grid_reliability_benchmarks.notes: ERCOT target 13.75% reserve margin. LOLE 1-in-10 standard (0.1 days/year). Battery storage improving effective reserve margins.
